brief.situation: You maintain dedupe.py at Wrenfield Regional Library Network (fictional). It keeps the first occurrence of each email address. After two library systems merged, the list grew from 200,000 to 2 million records, and the job no longer finishes overnight. Tonight's run starts at 22:00. It is 21:05.
handover: Output order must match input order (first occurrence kept).
The server has 16 GB of memory free; 2 million emails take about 200 MB as a set.
howItWorks: Pick a step from the action list: look, change, check or ship. Nothing you pick is typed or executed: every step shows an authored result.
Each step takes working minutes, and the clock moves by the minutes it takes. The deadline runs on the same clock.
Shipping is final for this case. Afterwards you record what you found and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the systems lead: why the job slowed, what you changed, and how you know.

parts.label: Why
parts.criteria: The loop runs n times and each list lookup is O(n), so the job is O(n squared): 10 times the data, about 100 times the time.
parts.modelAnswer: Quadratic: a list scan inside a loop.

parts.label: What you changed
parts.criteria: A set gives O(1) average lookups, so O(n) time for O(n) extra space; sorting is O(n log n) but loses order; parallelism divides a quadratic by a constant.

parts.label: How you know
parts.criteria: Timings on growing inputs are linear, the full run takes seconds, and output matches.

scoring.modelReasoning: Data grew 10-fold and run time about 100-fold: quadratic. Timing 50k, 100k and 200k confirms it, since doubling n quadruples time. The loop runs n times and 'not in' on a list is O(n). Track seen emails in a set, O(1) on average, which makes the job O(n) time for O(n) space and keeps order. Sorting is n log n but changes order; eight processes divide a quadratic by eight and miss duplicates across chunks.
